title: Control flow in the template: @if, @for and @switch

videos.script:
A template has to decide things. Whether to show a message. How many times to repeat a row. Which of several labels to draw. {{if}} Today you learn the blocks that do it, starting with at-if. It does not hide what is false. It removes it from the page.

{{for}} Then at-for, which repeats a block for every item in a list. The planner's courses appear on the week screen. At-for insists on one thing, called track. {{track}} You see why, on a bench. You type a number next to one course, reverse the list, and watch the number follow its course. Then you track by position instead, and the number stays behind, next to the wrong course.

{{switch}} At-switch picks one case out of several. And with one line, at-default never, the build refuses a case nobody wrote.

{{old}} Last, the code you will meet at work, written with star-ng-if and star-ng-for. You write some, and Angular's migration rewrites it into today's blocks. Then you read what it wrote, because it is correct, and still worth tidying.
